priorStories.headline: Germany arrests former spy chief in secrets case
priorStories.body:
German authorities arrested August Hanning, a former head of the country’s foreign intelligence service, and former intelligence official Manfred D.

Federal prosecutors allege that Manfred D. supplied Hanning with about 2,000 documents, including classified material. They say Hanning used some of the intelligence to prepare an analysis for an officer of an unidentified foreign intelligence service.

The allegations have not been adjudicated.

priorStories.headline: Kenya confirms fatal imported Bundibugyo virus case
priorStories.body:
Kenya confirmed that a citizen who returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo had Bundibugyo virus disease and died in a Nairobi hospital. It is Kenya’s first imported case linked to the current outbreak in Congo.

Authorities began tracing the person’s contacts and screening travelers. The confirmation does not by itself establish that the virus has spread within Kenya.

sources.name: World Health Organization Regional Office for Africa

priorStories.headline: Francis Halzen wins Nobel Prize in Physics
priorStories.body:
The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics to Francis Halzen for his contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos from beyond Earth.

IceCube uses sensors embedded deep in Antarctic ice to detect rare neutrino interactions. Those observations help researchers study distant, highly energetic processes that are difficult to examine using light alone.

candidates.summary: Interpol reported that Operation Madre Tierra VIII led to 233 arrests across nine Latin American and Caribbean countries. The June-July operation targeted illegal logging, mining and wildlife trafficking; authorities also recovered more than 1,000 live animals and identified about 60,000 hectares of illegally cleared forest.
candidates.title: Interpol reports 233 arrests in regional environmental crime operation

candidates.summary: NASA said the SpaceX Crew-12 Dragon undocked from the International Space Station with NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, European Space Agency astronaut Sophie Adenot and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev aboard. The departure began the crew’s return journey after a mission lasting nearly eight months.
candidates.title: SpaceX Crew-12 departs International Space Station

candidates.summary: Izmir Mayor Cemil Tugay joined Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s Justice and Development Party, giving the party the mayoralty of Turkey’s third-largest city and a longtime opposition stronghold. Tugay had left the Republican People’s Party in June and served as an independent. Izmir’s municipal assembly remains controlled by the opposition New Party.
candidates.title: Izmir mayor joins Erdogan’s ruling party

candidates.summary: Polish authorities said a 19-year-old student attacked students, teachers and passersby with a sharp object at a vocational school in Ostroleka. Nine people were reported injured, none with life-threatening wounds, although one was seriously hurt. Police arrested the suspect near the school; authorities had not announced a suspected motive.
candidates.title: Nine injured in attack at Polish vocational school

candidates.summary: Minutes from the Federal Reserve’s September policy meeting indicated that officials expected another interest-rate increase would be needed before the end of 2026. The minutes were released on October 7.
candidates.title: Federal Reserve minutes point to another 2026 rate increase

candidates.summary: Federal prosecutors charged Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud, 18, with receiving a firearm and ammunition to commit a federal terrorism crime. Authorities allege that he planned an ISIS-inspired mass shooting at the Mall of America on October 24. The FBI arrested him on October 6 after an undercover transaction involving an inert rifle; he made his initial court appearance on October 7. The allegations have not been adjudicated.
candidates.title: Minnesota man charged in alleged Mall of America attack plot

candidates.summary: Construction began in Fort Worth on the planned National Juneteenth Museum during events marking activist Opal Lee’s 100th birthday. The planned 50,000-square-foot museum is projected to open in 2029. Organizers also announced a $3 million donation from the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
candidates.title: Construction begins on National Juneteenth Museum
